slides.title: Rawafid Schools Group and Wafi, its parent-enquiry assistant
slides.text: One case all week Rawafid Schools Group and Wafi, its parent-enquiry assistant A fictional private school group: four campuses, about 1,200 students, parents who write in Arabic and English. Its systems lead built Wafi (وافي), which drafts replies from attendance and fee records with a language model. Dr. Amal Al-Sayari Group director of schools. Owns the build and its risks. Nasser Al-Mansour Data protection officer. Your client this week. Dana Al-Saleh Systems lead. Built Wafi fast, and it shows.

slides.title: Read the official text, then turn it into code and records
slides.text: How this course works Read the official text, then turn it into code and records Primary sources Every rule on a slide comes from the instrument itself, named in the notes. Commentary is not a source. Evidence, not opinion A finding is a number from a lab run: fields sent, names re-identified, a gap between languages. Synthetic data only No real person enters any lab, prompt or assistant. That is what lets us use a free hosted model. AI policy. AI off for the scenario check and each first classification. An assistant may help you read the instruments; check every answer against the official text. No real personal data in any assistant.

slides.title: Personal data and the law
slides.text: Today Personal data and the law Session 1 · Where personal data flows in a build Prompts, logs, caches and the model provider are all places where personal data goes Session 2 · Lawful basis and minimisation Every flow needs a legal basis and a purpose, and every field must earn its place against that purpose Session 3 · Pseudonymisation and its limits A pseudonym hides a name, not a person: quasi-identifiers link records back Session 4 · Rights, retention and breaches Rights, retention rules and the breach procedure turn the law into dates and duties

slides.title: Where personal data flows in a build
slides.text: Session 1 Where personal data flows in a build Identify the personal and sensitive data a build reads, sends, logs and stores Draw a data flow diagram of an AI assistant with every store and external party Name the PDPL obligation that applies at each step of the flow 01

slides.title: Personal data is anything that can identify a person, directly or not
slides.text: The law's starting point Personal data is anything that can identify a person, directly or not Directly: a name, a national ID number, a mobile number. Indirectly: a campus, a grade and a date of birth together. Sensitive data is a named list in the law: racial or ethnic origin, beliefs, criminal and security data, biometric and genetic data, health data, and data showing a parent is unknown. It applies to processing in the Kingdom, and from abroad for people living here. At Rawafid A note "asthma flare" on an absence is health data about a child. So is "insulin at lunch" in a student file.

slides.title: The controller decides, the processor acts for it, the data subject has the rights
slides.text: Three roles The controller decides, the processor acts for it, the data subject has the rights Role In the law At Rawafid Controller Decides why and how data is processed; carries the obligations Rawafid Schools Group Processor Processes for the controller; chosen only if it gives the necessary guarantees The model provider, the hosting company Data subject The person the data is about, or their legal guardian Each student, represented by a guardian; each guardian A minor's rights are exercised by the guardian, and the guardian's authority must be verified.

slides.title: Prompts, logs and caches are stores of personal data too
slides.text: Where an AI build keeps data Prompts, logs and caches are stores of personal data too Records The systems the build reads: students, guardians, attendance, fees. Prompts Everything the build sends to the model leaves your systems. Logs Often the full prompt and the reply, kept "for debugging", for ever. Caches and queues Replies kept for reuse; drafts waiting for staff. What goes wrong. Teams map the database and forget the log. The log usually holds more personal data per row than any table.

slides.title: One parent message passes through nine steps
slides.text: The build as Dana wrote it One parent message passes through nine steps 1 · Intake mobile and message → 2 to 4 · Look up guardian, child, attendance, fees → 5 · Prompt to the model provider → 6 · Draft back from the model → 7 to 9 · Keep review queue, log, cache Lab 1.1 runs one enquiry through this pipeline with a tracer that records every field at every step.

slides.title: One question about absences sends 21 fields out of Rawafid
slides.text: Measured in Lab 1.1 One question about absences sends 21 fields out of Rawafid 21 fields in one prompt 8 of them identifiers 1 sensitive: the health notes The prompt carries the whole student record, the guardian's name, national ID and mobile, and three counts. The question needed one count.

slides.title: A data flow diagram shows every place data goes and what goes there
slides.text: The tool for this session A data flow diagram shows every place data goes and what goes there flowchart LR Wafi([Wafi]) ModelProvider["model provider"] WafiEnquiryLog["Wafi enquiry log"] Wafi -->|"5 send prompt: send 21"| ModelProvider Wafi -->|"8 log: log 4"| WafiEnquiryLog Nodes: the build, each store, each outside party. Edges: one per step, labelled with what moves. Annotate each edge with the obligation that applies there. Mermaid is text: it lives in the repository and changes with the code. draw.io is the drawing alternative.

slides.title: Each step of the flow carries its own obligation
slides.text: From diagram to duties Each step of the flow carries its own obligation Step Obligation (Personal Data Protection Law) Intake Tell the guardian the basis, the purpose and who receives the data (Article 13) Look up A legal basis and purpose (Articles 5, 6, 10); accuracy (Article 14) Prompt Minimum content (Article 11); security (Article 19); transfer abroad (Article 29) Draft Accuracy before anything is sent to the guardian (Article 14) Log and cache Destruction when no longer needed (Article 18); security (Article 19) Whole activity A record of processing (Article 31)

slides.title: Which store did Dana forget?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which store did Dana forget? Dana's data map lists the student system, the fee system and the model provider. Wafi writes every prompt to its enquiry log. What does the map miss? Nothing: the provider is the only other store The log, which holds the full prompt of every enquiry Only debug output, which the law does not cover The cache, but caches hold no personal data

slides.title: Trace Wafi's personal data
slides.text: Lab 1.1 · 25 min Trace Wafi's personal data Map every field the assistant reads, sends, logs and stores on a data flow diagram. D1_1_map_every_field.ipynb Run one enquiry through the instrumented Wafi 4 min List every field read, sent, logged and stored 7 min Flag the identifiers and the sensitive fields 4 min Draw the data flow diagram in Mermaid 5 min Name the PDPL obligation at each step 5 min ✱ Stretch: Add the hosted provider's own logs as a store you do not control

slides.title: Lawful basis and minimisation
slides.text: Session 2 Lawful basis and minimisation Choose a legal basis and a purpose for each flow of a build Test each field against the purpose and remove what it does not need Rewrite a prompt builder so it sends the minimum 02

slides.title: Consent is the default; the law lists when processing runs without it
slides.text: The rule and its exceptions Consent is the default; the law lists when processing runs without it Consent (Article 5) No processing and no change of purpose without the data subject's consent, which can be withdrawn at any time. For a minor, the guardian consents. Without consent (Article 6) The data subject's actual interest when contact is impossible; another law or an agreement the data subject is party to; a public entity's security or judicial needs; the controller's legitimate interest. The catch Legitimate interest never covers sensitive data.

slides.title: Each flow gets its own basis and purpose
slides.text: Wafi's five flows Each flow gets its own basis and purpose Flow Basis Purpose F1 · answer the guardian contract The enrolment contract the guardian signed F2 · draft with a model contract The provider acts as processor for F1 F3 · keep a log legitimate interest Quality and complaints, without sensitive data F4 · cache replies legitimate interest Avoid repeated model calls F5 · add summer-camp offers consent Advertising needs prior consent and a way to stop

slides.title: The purpose decides which fields may be collected and sent
slides.text: Minimisation The purpose decides which fields may be collected and sent The purpose must relate directly to the controller's purposes (Article 11). Content is limited to the minimum the purpose needs. Data not needed any more is no longer collected, and what was collected is destroyed. Data is processed only for the purpose it was collected for, with listed exceptions (Article 10). The guideline's test, per field Actual need, purpose, method of collection, content, destruction, retention. If a field fails "actual need", it goes.

slides.title: Five of the 21 fields are needed to answer the question
slides.text: Measured in Lab 1.2 Five of the 21 fields are needed to answer the question Keep The child's first name, absences this term, late arrivals this term, the fee balance, the message. Drop: 16 fields Both national IDs, the guardian's mobile and name, date of birth, nationality, campus, section, bus route, health notes and the internal IDs. Before 678 characters After 286 characters

slides.title: Send facts, not records
slides.text: The change in code Send facts, not records name = (student["full_name_ar"] if is_arabic(text) else student["full_name"]).split()[0] data = {"first_name": name, **facts} # three counts, nothing else prompt = ("You are Wafi ... using only these facts.\n" f"Facts: {json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False)}\n" f"Guardian message: {text}") Pattern. Compute what the question needs inside your systems; send the answer's ingredients, never the source rows.

slides.title: For a child, the guardian consents and exercises the rights
slides.text: A school's special case For a child, the guardian consents and exercises the rights When a data subject lacks full legal capacity, the legal guardian acts in the child's best interest. The controller takes appropriate steps to verify the guardianship before relying on it. The guardian's consent may not harm the child's interests. When the child reaches legal capacity, they exercise their rights themselves. What goes wrong. Wafi finds the family by mobile number. A number shared between two families, or a parent without custody, gets another child's data.

slides.title: Can the log run on legitimate interest?
slides.text: Checkpoint Can the log run on legitimate interest? Dana says the enquiry log runs on Rawafid's legitimate interest in quality checks. The log keeps full prompts, health notes included. Is that basis available? Yes: quality checking is a legitimate interest Yes: the enrolment contract covers all of Wafi No: every flow needs the guardian's consent No: legitimate interest excludes sensitive data

slides.title: Lawful basis and minimum fields
slides.text: Lab 1.2 · 25 min Lawful basis and minimum fields Set a lawful basis and purpose for each flow and remove the fields the purpose does not need. D1_2_set_lawful_basis.ipynb Set a basis and purpose for each of the five flows 6 min Test each prompt field against the purpose 6 min Write the minimised prompt builder 7 min Check ten prompts and print the before-and-after list 6 min ✱ Stretch: Draft the consent wording for the one optional flow

slides.title: Pseudonymisation and its limits
slides.text: Session 3 Pseudonymisation and its limits Pseudonymise identifiers with a keyed hash and keep the key apart Attempt re-identification by joining on quasi-identifiers Generalise quasi-identifiers and measure the remaining risk 03

slides.title: Minimised, pseudonymised and anonymised are three different promises
slides.text: Three words people mix up Minimised, pseudonymised and anonymised are three different promises Minimised Fewer fields. What is left still identifies the person. Pseudonymised Identifiers replaced by codes; the extra information that links back is kept apart. Still personal data. Anonymised Irreversibly unidentifiable, directly and indirectly. Outside the law, once tested for re-identification.

slides.title: Use a keyed hash, and keep the key away from the data
slides.text: How to pseudonymise Use a keyed hash, and keep the key away from the data def code(value, key): mac = hmac.new(key.encode(), value.encode(), hashlib.sha256) return "P" + mac.hexdigest()[:10] out = df.drop(columns=["full_name", "full_name_ar", "national_id"]) out["student_id"] = out["student_id"].map( lambda v: code(v, KEY)) Same person, same code: joins across files still work. Without the key nobody can recompute a code. A plain hash is not a pseudonym: anyone can hash every student number and look it up.

slides.title: Quasi-identifiers link a record back to a name
slides.text: The attacker's tool Quasi-identifiers link a record back to a name Pseudonymised file campus, grade, gender, date of birth, health notes → Join on the four shared columns ← Public page sports-day results: name, campus, grade, gender, date of birth No single column identifies a child. Together they almost always do.

slides.title: A join re-identifies 96% of the names on the sports-day page
slides.text: Measured in Lab 1.3 A join re-identifies 96% of the names on the sports-day page 308 / 320 page names matched to one record 26 children whose health note is now known 0 names in the pseudonymised file What goes wrong. "We removed the names" is the most common description of a file that is still personal data.

slides.title: Generalising cuts the attack to almost nothing, and leaves the rare child exposed
slides.text: The fix, and its limit Generalising cuts the attack to almost nothing, and leaves the rare child exposed Exact birth date and grade 96% Birth year and grade band 0.3% Birth date becomes birth year; grade becomes a band of three. One page name still matches one record. The smallest group holds one child: k = 1. 33 of 121 groups hold fewer than five children.

slides.title: Claim anonymity only after you have tried to break it
slides.text: The rule for any release Claim anonymity only after you have tried to break it 1 · Remove direct identifiers → 2 · Attack join with what is public → 3 · Generalise and suppress small groups → 4 · Measure rate and k, written down Your evidence for LO4: the before-and-after field list, the pseudonymisation script and the re-identification result.

slides.title: Is the contractor's file still personal data?
slides.text: Checkpoint Is the contractor's file still personal data? Dana sends a contractor the student file with names and national IDs removed and student numbers replaced by HMAC codes. Rawafid keeps the key. Under the PDPL guidelines, what is the file? Personal data, because it can be linked back Anonymous data, because no names remain Outside the law, because the codes are encrypted Personal data only while Rawafid holds it

slides.title: Pseudonymise, then attack
slides.text: Lab 1.3 · 25 min Pseudonymise, then attack Pseudonymise the guardian and student records and attempt to re-identify them by linkage. D1_3_pseudonymise_guardian_student.ipynb Replace identifiers with keyed pseudonyms 6 min Join with the sports-day page on quasi-identifiers 6 min Measure the re-identification rate 4 min Generalise birth date and grade, measure again 6 min Record k and the residual risk 3 min ✱ Stretch: Show that an unkeyed hash of a student number is reversed by trying every number

slides.title: Rights, retention and breaches
slides.text: Session 4 Rights, retention and breaches Explain the data subject's rights and who exercises them for a minor Write a retention rule per store and find what is kept too long Walk a breach through notice, containment and documentation 04

slides.title: Five rights, answered within 30 days
slides.text: What the data subject may ask Five rights, answered within 30 days To be told the legal basis and purpose. To access their data. To obtain it in a readable, clear format. To have it corrected, completed or updated. To have it destroyed when no longer needed. 30 days to act on a request, extendable by 30 with notice and reasons For Wafi A guardian's request covers the log and the cache, not only the student system.

slides.title: Destroy data once its purpose is met, unless a law says keep it
slides.text: Retention Destroy data once its purpose is met, unless a law says keep it Destroy without undue delay once the purpose no longer needs the data (Article 18). Keep it only for a legal basis with a set period, or a case before a court. Data with nothing that identifies the person may be kept. Destroy every copy, backups included, and tell those you disclosed it to. A rule has three parts Period (90 days), start (the date of the enquiry), method (scheduled deletion of rows and backups).

slides.title: Under a 90-day rule, 78% of Wafi's log should not exist
slides.text: Measured in Lab 1.4 Under a 90-day rule, 78% of Wafi's log should not exist 1,027 of 1,315 log rows older than 90 days The oldest row is from the pilot's first week, 2025-09-14. Each row holds a full prompt: a child's record. The rule is 60 days for complaints to arrive plus 30 to investigate them.

slides.title: A breach has three stages: notify, contain, document
slides.text: The breach guide A breach has three stages: notify, contain, document 1 · Notify SDAIA within 72 hours of becoming aware, when harm is expected → 2 · Contain stop it, change what can be changed, tell the data subjects → 3 · Document keep the notice, the actions and the lessons The clock starts at awareness, not on the day of the breach and not when the investigation ends.

slides.title: Five contents, written while the clock runs
slides.text: What the notice to SDAIA holds Five contents, written while the clock runs Content For Rawafid's incident 1 What happened, when, how, and when you became aware Log export on a shared drive; found 2026-11-09 2 Categories and numbers of data subjects; kinds of data 434 students, 396 guardians; IDs, health notes 3 Risks, remedial actions, measures against recurrence Link removed; prompts minimised; log at 90 days 4 Whether data subjects are or will be notified Yes, without undue delay 5 Contact of the controller or its DPO Nasser Al-Mansour

slides.title: A record of processing lists what you have just mapped
slides.text: The record that ties it together A record of processing lists what you have just mapped Controller and DPO contacts; the purpose. Categories of data subjects and of data. Who receives it; transfers outside the Kingdom. Retention period per category; security measures. Kept in writing, up to date Available to the competent authority on request, and kept five years after the activity ends.

slides.title: When must Rawafid have notified SDAIA?
slides.text: Checkpoint When must Rawafid have notified SDAIA? The export went on the shared drive on 2026-10-21. Dana found the public link and told the DPO on 2026-11-09. Harm to the children is expected. By when must SDAIA be notified? By 2026-10-24, three days after the upload When the investigation is finished Within 72 hours of 2026-11-09, so by 2026-11-12 Only if someone is shown to have misused the data

slides.title: Retention and a seeded breach
slides.text: Lab 1.4 · 25 min Retention and a seeded breach Write a retention rule per store and walk a seeded breach through the PDPL breach guideline. D1_4_write_retention_rule.ipynb Write a retention rule per store 6 min Count log rows past the rule 4 min Read the incident and size the breach 5 min Draft the notice to SDAIA with its five contents 6 min Decide the notice to guardians 4 min ✱ Stretch: Add the breach to the documentation record with its corrective actions

slides.title: Map everything, send the minimum, and test before you call it anonymous
slides.text: Day 1 · Three things to keep Map everything, send the minimum, and test before you call it anonymous The log is a store Prompts, logs, caches and the provider all hold personal data, with all the obligations. Facts, not records One question needed 5 of 21 fields. Basis and purpose decide which. Pseudonymised is personal 96% came back by a join. Measure k, write it down, and keep the key apart.

slides.title: Classify, share and send
slides.text: SDAIA Academy · Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom Classify, share and send Day 2: Classify each data set, decide where it may go, and check what you reuse Data & AI Foundations Track3 teaching days + capstone day4 sessions · 4 labsFN-106

slides.title: Classify, share and send
slides.text: Today Classify, share and send Session 1 · Data classification levels Classification follows the impact of disclosure: four levels, and sub-levels inside Restricted Session 2 · What may reach an external model The classification level decides whether data may go to a hosted model, a locally served one, or neither Session 3 · Sharing with another entity A request to share data is judged on purpose, minimum data, access, transparency and destruction Session 4 · Licences and provenance Weights, code and data each carry terms, and each instrument decides a different question

slides.title: Which change does the most for Wafi's log?
slides.text: Review of Day 1 Which change does the most for Wafi's log? Wafi's log keeps every full prompt since the pilot began. Nasser can make one change this week. Which one reduces the exposure the most? Encrypt the log file on disk Remove the names from old rows Send minimised prompts and delete rows past 90 days Add the log to the privacy notice

slides.title: Data classification levels
slides.text: Session 1 Data classification levels Assess the impact category and level of a data set's disclosure Assign a classification level with an evidence-based reason Spot aggregates that still reveal individuals 01

slides.title: A classification level is a decision about handling, made once
slides.text: What classification is for A classification level is a decision about handling, made once Every data set gets a level when it is created or received. The level decides access, storage, sharing, publication and, today, which model may see it. Data not yet classified is treated as Restricted until it is. The level is reviewed within a month of the first classification. Whose policy? The NDMO Data Classification Policy is written for public entities. Rawafid, a private group, adopts it in its own data policy; the PDPL binds it by law.

slides.title: The level follows the impact of unauthorised disclosure
slides.text: Four levels The level follows the impact of unauthorised disclosure Level Impact Example in the policy Top Secret High: exceptionally serious, irreparable National security information Secret Medium: serious Information on vital installations Restricted Low: limited Personal identifiers, a medical file, individual transactions Public None Published statistics, public announcements Restricted has sub-levels by scale: A a whole sector, B several entities or a group of individuals, C one entity or one individual.

slides.title: Ask what disclosure would harm, then how badly and for how long
slides.text: How to assess impact Ask what disclosure would harm, then how badly and for how long National interest Reputation, security, economy, infrastructure, government functions. Entity activities Profits and functions of entities. Individuals Health and safety; privacy. Environment Environmental and natural resources. The level weighs the duration of the damage, the time to recover and its scale. Every impact named must be specific and evidence-based.

slides.title: A low impact still has two questions before it becomes a level
slides.text: The policy's process A low impact still has two questions before it becomes a level Impact Low limited, short-term, controllable → Step 4 Would disclosure break a law? Yes: Restricted → Step 5 Do the benefits outweigh the harm? Yes: Public. No: Restricted Open by default. The two steps exist so that data is not locked away when nothing forbids its release.

slides.title: A set built from several levels takes the highest of them
slides.text: Combining data A set built from several levels takes the highest of them Principle 4 · highest level of protection If a data set integrates parts with different levels, the highest level applies. At Rawafid The fee schedule (Public) joined with each family's balance (Restricted) is Restricted. So is a prompt that carries one Restricted field.

slides.title: An aggregate table can still describe one child
slides.text: Measured in Lab 2.1 An aggregate table can still describe one child 12 / 95 cells of the attendance summary hold fewer than five students Each cell is campus, grade and gender, with an absence rate. A cell of one student is that student's attendance. Until small cells are suppressed or merged, the table is Restricted.

slides.title: Six sets, two levels, one reason each
slides.text: The register Six sets, two levels, one reason each Set Level Reason fee_schedule Public Already published guardians Restricted B Names, national IDs, mobiles, IBANs students Restricted B Children's identities and health notes attendance Restricted B Absences, with notes that can reveal health fees Restricted B Detailed statements of individual transactions attendance_summary Restricted B Cells under five students

slides.title: What level does Dana's new report take?
slides.text: Checkpoint What level does Dana's new report take? Dana joins the published fee schedule with each family's balance to show who is behind on payments. What is the report's level? Restricted, the higher of its two parts Somewhere between Public and Restricted Public, because the fees are published Unclassified until someone reviews it

slides.title: Classify six data sets
slides.text: Lab 2.1 · 25 min Classify six data sets Classify the six data sets with the policy's impact categories and record the reasons. D2_1_classify_six_data.ipynb Read the inventory and the impact categories 4 min Assess impact category and level per set 8 min Map impact to level and sub-level 5 min Find the small cells in the aggregate table 5 min Record reasons in the register 3 min ✱ Stretch: Suppress the small cells and classify the aggregate table again

slides.title: What may reach an external model
slides.text: Session 2 What may reach an external model Derive a destination rule from the classification level and the data's nature Apply the rule to data sets and to the fields of a prompt Recognise a hosted endpoint abroad as a transfer outside the Kingdom 02

slides.title: Three destinations: a hosted service, a model you run, or no model
slides.text: Where a prompt can go Three destinations: a hosted service, a model you run, or no model Hosted A provider's model over an API. Fast to start; the data leaves you, under the provider's terms and location. Locally served An open-weight model on your own machines in the Kingdom. The data stays under your controls. Neither Some data has no business in a prompt at all. Minimisation decides before any model does.

slides.title: Generative AI tools get Public data only
slides.text: What the guidelines say Generative AI tools get Public data only The Generative AI Guidelines for Government: do not enter data classified Restricted or higher into generative AI tools. Limit their use to data classified Public; check the tool's privacy, disclosure and sharing terms. Data analysis with generative AI is limited to Public or open data sets. Rawafid's reading The rule covers hosted services Rawafid does not control. A model Rawafid runs itself, under the source system's access rules, may see minimised Restricted fields.

slides.title: Three lines turn a level into a destination
slides.text: The rule as code Three lines turn a level into a destination def destination(level, has_sensitive): if level == "Public": return "hosted" if level == "Restricted" and not has_sensitive: return "local" return "neither" Pseudonymised data keeps its Restricted level, so pseudonymising does not change the answer.

slides.title: Only the published fee schedule may go to a hosted model
slides.text: Measured in Lab 2.2 Only the published fee schedule may go to a hosted model fee_schedule hosted guardians, fees, summary local students, attendance neither Field by field, all five fields of the minimised prompt are Restricted: local only. Minimised is small, not Public.

slides.title: A hosted endpoint outside the Kingdom makes every prompt a transfer
slides.text: The other half of the question A hosted endpoint outside the Kingdom makes every prompt a transfer Transfer only for listed purposes, without harm to national security or vital interests. With an adequate level of protection abroad, and the minimum data needed. Otherwise safeguards: standard contractual clauses, binding common rules or a certificate. Location unknown? Treat it as abroad. If you cannot show where prompts are processed, you cannot show the conditions are met.

slides.title: Synthetic records describe nobody, so they may go anywhere
slides.text: Why the class may use a hosted model Synthetic records describe nobody, so they may go anywhere In class synthetic records, hosted free model → The gate before real records: classify again → In production Restricted fields, local model only What goes wrong. A prototype built on a hosted model is pointed at real data "just for a test". The test is the breach.

slides.title: Does pseudonymising open the hosted route?
slides.text: Checkpoint Does pseudonymising open the hosted route? Dana pseudonymises attendance counts with a keyed hash and asks to send them to the free hosted model for a monthly summary. Under Rawafid's rule, where may they go? To the hosted model, now that they are pseudonymised To the hosted model, because Rawafid keeps the key Nowhere: attendance data can never reach a model To a locally served model only

slides.title: Hosted, local or neither
slides.text: Lab 2.2 · 25 min Hosted, local or neither Decide for each data set whether it may go to a hosted model, a locally served model or neither. D2_2_decide_each_data.ipynb Write the destination rule as a function 7 min Apply it to the six data sets 4 min Apply it field by field to Wafi's prompt 6 min Check the hosted endpoint's location as a transfer 4 min Record the permitted destinations 4 min ✱ Stretch: Write the rule for the synthetic class data and say why it differs

slides.title: Sharing with another entity
slides.text: Session 3 Sharing with another entity Assess a data request against the Data Sharing Policy principles Cut a request down to the minimum data its purpose needs Draft the conditions under which data may be shared 03

slides.title: A research centre asks for three years of attendance, with names
slides.text: The request A research centre asks for three years of attendance, with names Purpose: commute distance and absence in primary and middle school. Fields: names, national IDs, birth dates, district, guardian's employer, daily records, absence notes, health notes. Storage: a cloud workspace outside the Kingdom. Retention: indefinitely; onward: research partners when needed. The decision Not yes or no: what, in which form, on what conditions.

slides.title: Eight principles decide whether and how data is shared
slides.text: The Data Sharing Policy Eight principles decide whether and how data is shared Sharing culture Share by default, under the policy. Single source The entity that produces data shares it. Legitimate purpose A legal basis; used only for that purpose. Authorised access Identified, verified people. Transparency Data, level, storage, protection, destruction. Accountability Shared, under an agreement. Security Controls per the national rules. Ethical use Fairness, integrity, trust.

slides.title: The PDPL allows research sharing when the data does not identify the child
slides.text: The law's side The PDPL allows research sharing when the data does not identify the child Disclosure (Article 15) Only in listed cases, among them consent, and later processing in a form that cannot identify the data subject directly or indirectly. Research (Article 27) Without consent when the data does not specifically identify the person, or identity evidence is destroyed first and the data is not sensitive. The health notes fail both. They are sensitive and they identify; a commute study does not need them.

slides.title: Six of eleven requested fields survive, in a coarser form
slides.text: Measured in Lab 2.3 Six of eleven requested fields survive, in a coarser form Requested Shared as date of birth birth year grade grade band, grades 1 to 9 only gender, campus, district as they are daily attendance records absence counts per month names, national IDs, employer, notes, health notes refused

slides.title: The field the study needs most makes the smallest groups
slides.text: The trade-off in the extract The field the study needs most makes the smallest groups k = 2 with the district: 4 of 96 groups under five k = 11 without it: no group under five Share the district and suppress or merge the small groups before release. Or compute commute bands inside Rawafid and share those instead of the district. Either way, write the choice into the conditions.

slides.title: Yes, on nine conditions
slides.text: The answer to the centre Yes, on nine conditions The stated study only. The pseudonymised extract, coarse fields. Labelled Restricted in the metadata. Stored in the Kingdom, or a lawful transfer. Named researchers only. No onward sharing. Destroyed at the end, with a signed confirmation. A secure channel, not email. An agreement signed before any data moves.

slides.title: Is "for research" enough?
slides.text: Checkpoint Is "for research" enough? The centre says the purpose is research, so every requested field should be shared. What does the Data Sharing Policy's legitimate-purpose principle add? Nothing: research is always a legitimate purpose The data is used only for the stated purpose, and fields beyond it are not shared Only public entities may receive data Data must be stored on the requester's own servers

slides.title: Licences and provenance
slides.text: Session 4 Licences and provenance Read the licence of a model and of a dataset from its card Record use restrictions and obligations in a licence register Name the national instrument that decides a given question 04

slides.title: Weights, code and data each carry their own terms
slides.text: What you reuse Weights, code and data each carry their own terms Weights An open-source licence, or the vendor's own terms with a use policy. Code Usually a standard licence in the repository. Data Often Creative Commons, and with a provenance of its own. Open weights are not public domain. Downloadable does not mean free of conditions.

slides.title: An SPDX identifier names one exact licence text
slides.text: A shared vocabulary An SPDX identifier names one exact licence text Licence SPDX identifier Apache License 2.0 Apache-2.0 Creative Commons Attribution Non Commercial 4.0 CC-BY-NC-4.0 A vendor's own terms LicenseRef- and a name A register, a scanner and a lawyer then mean the same thing. Cards on model hubs carry a licence tag; read the licence file it points to. Record the date you checked: terms change.

slides.title: Two models and one dataset, three different answers
slides.text: Read in Lab 2.4 Two models and one dataset, three different answers Artefact Licence For Wafi Qwen3-4B (weights) Apache-2.0 Yes : keep the licence and notices Gemma 3 4B IT (weights) Gemma Terms of Use Yes, with conditions : use policy, notice file, pass restrictions on Alpaca (dataset) CC-BY-NC-4.0 No : non-commercial, English only, generated by another company's model

slides.title: Provenance asks where the content came from, and what came with it
slides.text: Beyond the licence Provenance asks where the content came from, and what came with it Who made it , from what: a dataset generated by another model may carry that model's terms and errors. Which languages : an English-only dataset will not teach Gulf Arabic replies. What is inside : personal data in training text is still personal data. When you checked , and where the record of it lives.

slides.title: Publishing open data means classifying it Public first, then licensing it
slides.text: Licences in the other direction Publishing open data means classifying it Public first, then licensing it Open data is a subset of Public data: classify first, publish second. Open by default, unless the data needs protection. Machine-readable (CSV, JSON), free of charge, no registration. Released under a licence that states the conditions of reuse. At Rawafid The fee schedule can be published today. The attendance summary only after its small cells are suppressed and it is classified again. The sports-day page was published with dates of birth: Lab 1.3 showed what that cost.

slides.title: Each instrument decides its own question
slides.text: Closing the day Each instrument decides its own question Instrument Decides Data Classification Policy The level of a data set, and who reviews it Data Sharing Policy Whether and on what conditions data goes to another entity Open Data Policy How Public data is released for anyone to reuse Generative AI Guidelines What may enter a generative AI tool, and what users are told Personal Data Protection Law Everything about personal data, whichever policy also applies

Rawafid is a fee-charging private school group. What does the licence allow? Any use, since it is public on the hub Any use, with attribution No use in Rawafid's commercial service Use only after classifying it as Public

slides.title: The level decides where data may go; the purpose decides what goes
slides.text: Day 2 · Three things to keep The level decides where data may go; the purpose decides what goes Level first Classify by impact; the highest level of the parts wins; unclassified is Restricted. Hosted is a choice Only Public data goes to a hosted model. Real records need a model you run. Yes, on conditions Sharing and reuse are decided field by field and term by term, and written down.

slides.title: Ethics and risk in practice
slides.text: Today Ethics and risk in practice Session 1 · Principles into tests A principle becomes useful when it is a check with a threshold that passes or fails Session 2 · Testing the assistant Paired enquiries in Arabic and English show whether the assistant serves both groups equally Session 3 · Risk tier and risk register The ethics tier sets the bar; the national framework rates, treats and reviews each risk Session 4 · Disclosure and human review Parents are told what the assistant is and does, and sensitive replies go to a person

slides.title: Where may Wafi's minimised prompt go?
slides.text: Review of Day 2 Where may Wafi's minimised prompt go? After Lab 1.2 Wafi's prompt carries a child's first name, three counts and the guardian's message. Under Rawafid's rule, where may that prompt go with real records? To the free hosted model, since it is minimised To a model served inside Rawafid only Nowhere: it describes a child To any hosted model whose terms forbid training on it

slides.title: Principles into tests
slides.text: Session 1 Principles into tests Translate an ethics principle into a measurable check Set a threshold and a pass rule for each check Run checks over a recorded run and read the failures 01

slides.title: Seven principles, and three of them can be tested today
slides.text: The AI Ethics Principles Seven principles, and three of them can be tested today Fairness No bias, discrimination or stigma. Privacy and security Days 1 and 2. Humanity Human-centred, human oversight. Social and environmental benefits Serve people and the planet. Reliability and safety Works as specified, safely. Transparency and explainability People know and understand. Accountability and responsibility Someone answers for it.

slides.title: A principle becomes useful when it is a check that can fail
slides.text: From a word to a test A principle becomes useful when it is a check that can fail Principle "fair to all guardians" → Measure correct replies per language → Threshold gap at most 10 points, set first → Result pass or fail, with the cases to read The principle asks for this. Fairness metrics are chosen early, with a threshold that defines fair and unfair, and monitored in production.

slides.title: A recorded run: 24 replies from the pilot, with what each one did
slides.text: What the checks read A recorded run: 24 replies from the pilot, with what each one did Field Feeds language, sensitive, a reviewer's quality mark, escalated Fairness AI disclosure line, human route, sent Transparency model, prompt version, reviewed by Accountability If the log does not record a field, the principle that needs it cannot be checked.

slides.title: All three checks fail on the pilot's own log
slides.text: Measured in Lab 3.1 All three checks fail on the pilot's own log 58% / 100% replies marked correct, Arabic against English 2 of 24 replies sent without the AI notice 5 replies with no model, no reviewer or no escalation The two sensitive replies that were never escalated are both Arabic.

slides.title: Rates across groups need a tolerance; duties to each person do not
slides.text: Thresholds Rates across groups need a tolerance; duties to each person do not Fairness: ten points Rates move by chance across small groups. The gap is judged against a threshold set in advance. Transparency: zero Each guardian is owed the notice. One reply without it is one guardian misled. What goes wrong. A threshold written after the results are known is fitted to pass.

slides.title: Dana wants to change the threshold
slides.text: Checkpoint Dana wants to change the threshold The fairness check fails with a gap of 42 points. Dana proposes raising the threshold to 45 so the release can go ahead. What is wrong with that? Nothing, if the new threshold is written down Thresholds must always be five points The check only matters after release A threshold set after the results is fitted to pass

slides.title: Three checks
slides.text: Lab 3.1 · 25 min Three checks Write three checks that turn fairness, transparency and accountability into pass or fail results. D3_1_write_three_checks.ipynb Turn fairness into a measurable check with a threshold 8 min Turn transparency into a check on every reply 6 min Turn accountability into a check on the log 6 min Run all three on the recorded run 5 min ✱ Stretch: Add a fourth check for privacy: no identifier in any reply

slides.title: Testing the assistant
slides.text: Session 2 Testing the assistant Run a scripted test set through an assistant Compare reply quality and escalation rates per language Name the bias types that explain a measured gap 02

slides.title: Ask the same thing twice, once in each language
slides.text: How to test for a language gap Ask the same thing twice, once in each language Twenty enquiries guardians send, each in English and in Arabic. Arabic in the forms guardians write: Modern Standard and Gulf. Twelve routine questions with a known answer; eight sensitive ones that must reach a person. Same guardian, same child, same question: the only difference is the language. Example pair "Can you tell me Yousef's absences so far?" كم مرة غاب يوسف لين الحين؟

slides.title: A scripted stand-in gives everyone the same numbers
slides.text: The model behind the test A scripted stand-in gives everyone the same numbers Stand-in (default) Fixed templates filled from the prompt. It reads Modern Standard Arabic phrasings and misses Gulf ones, on purpose, so the method can be learned on a known gap. Free hosted model (optional) With a key, a real model drafts the replies. Results vary by model and day; synthetic data only. Say it plainly. The stand-in is not evidence about any real model. The method is what transfers.

slides.title: English is served fully; Gulf Arabic is served least
slides.text: Measured in Lab 3.2 English is served fully; Gulf Arabic is served least Variety Routine replies correct Sensitive enquiries escalated English 12 of 12 8 of 8 Modern Standard Arabic 6 of 6 2 of 4 Gulf Arabic 2 of 6 0 of 4

slides.title: A weak reply is visible; a missed escalation reaches nobody
slides.text: Which gap matters more A weak reply is visible; a missed escalation reaches nobody Routine reply wrong The guardian sees a generic answer and asks again or calls. Annoying, recoverable. Sensitive enquiry not escalated "Rahaf was unwell at school yesterday" gets a template reply and no person reads it. The school never knew.

slides.title: Three bias types explain what the test measured
slides.text: The AI Bias Reference Guide Three bias types explain what the test measured Bias type The guide's sense At Rawafid Language Trained on standard language, fails on dialect Gulf phrasings fail where MSA succeeds Evaluation Tests do not reflect the real users The pilot was tested in English only Automation People trust the system's output over their judgement Staff read only what the router flags

slides.title: Which bias type does the pilot's test show?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which bias type does the pilot's test show? Dana's pilot report said Wafi answered 100% of test enquiries correctly. Every test enquiry was in English. Which bias type from the national guide does the report show? Automation bias Evaluation bias Measurement bias Language bias

slides.text: Lab 3.2 · 25 min Forty enquiries Run forty scripted enquiries in Arabic and English, compare reply quality and escalation rates, and name the bias types from the national guide that explain any gap. D3_2_run_forty_scripted.ipynb Run the forty enquiries through Wafi 6 min Score reply quality per language 6 min Compare escalation rates per language 5 min Name the bias types that explain the gaps 5 min Write the test report rows 3 min ✱ Stretch: Rerun with the Arabic keywords added and measure the change

slides.title: Risk tier and risk register
slides.text: Session 3 Risk tier and risk register Place an AI system in an ethics risk tier with reasons Rate harms by likelihood and impact and compute the risk level Write a register entry with treatment, owner and review date 03

slides.title: Four risk levels set how much is required before use
slides.text: The AI Ethics Principles Four risk levels set how much is required before use Level What follows Little or no risk No restrictions; ethical compliance recommended Limited risk The AI ethics principles apply High risk Conformity assessments before and after deployment, and the statutory requirements Unacceptable risk Not allowed; examples include exploitation of children

slides.title: Limited risk, on one condition
slides.text: Placing Wafi Limited risk, on one condition Wafi answers factual questions; it decides nothing about a child. Health, safety, custody, complaints and disputed fees are meant to reach a person first. So the principles apply, and Wafi is tested against them. The condition If sensitive replies went out without review, or Wafi began to decide anything about a child, it would be high risk. Lab 3.2 showed the routing does not yet hold in Arabic.

slides.title: Set the context, then four phases that repeat
slides.text: The National AI Risk Management Framework Set the context, then four phases that repeat Context and scope the system, its users, the rules → Identify what could go wrong → Assess likelihood × impact → Treat avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept → Monitor and review re-rate, report It rests on four pillars: general principles, AI regulations, data regulations and sector regulations.

slides.title: Two four-point scales, multiplied, give four bands
slides.text: Assess Two four-point scales, multiplied, give four bands Likelihood Impact 1 Rare Low 2 Unlikely Medium 3 Likely High 4 Almost certain Catastrophic Level Band 1 to 2 Low 3 to 6 Medium 8 to 12 High 16 Catastrophic

slides.title: Three of five harms rate high before treatment
slides.text: Measured in Lab 3.3 Three of five harms rate high before treatment Harm L × I Band Owner After H1 wrong family's data 2 × 3 = 6 medium Dana Al-Saleh 3 medium H2 log leaks 2 × 4 = 8 high Nasser Al-Mansour 4 medium H3 Gulf Arabic served less 4 × 2 = 8 high Layla Haddad 4 medium H4 wrong number stated 3 × 2 = 6 medium Osama Al-Qurashi 2 low H5 drafts approved unread 3 × 3 = 9 high Dr. Amal Al-Sayari 6 medium

slides.title: Treatment lowers likelihood more easily than impact
slides.text: Treat, then rate again Treatment lowers likelihood more easily than impact H2 after treatment: 1 × 4 Minimised prompts and deletion after 90 days make a leak less likely and smaller. A leak of children's records is still catastrophic. Still high after treatment? Treat it further, or have someone with the authority accept it with a recorded reason, and escalate.

slides.title: Rate the new harm
slides.text: Checkpoint Rate the new harm Nasser adds a harm: an export of the full log, with health notes of 434 children, is shared outside Rawafid. He rates it unlikely (2) and catastrophic (4). What is its level and band? 6, medium Catastrophic, because the impact is catastrophic 8, high 4, medium

slides.title: Disclosure and human review
slides.text: Session 4 Disclosure and human review Draft a disclosure that names the assistant, the data and the human route Write a rule that sends sensitive replies to staff Test the rule for recall in both languages 04

slides.title: Three sources decide what the notice says
slides.text: What parents must be told Three sources decide what the notice says PDPL Article 13 Purpose and basis, how data is collected, who is responsible and how to reach them, recipients, rights. Generative AI Guidelines Say when content is made with generative AI; offer a channel that does not go through it. AI Ethics Principles Transparency, and humanity: a person reviews what matters.

slides.title: Two documents: one for government staff, one for everyone who builds or uses
slides.text: The Generative AI Guidelines Two documents: one for government staff, one for everyone who builds or uses For government Public data only in generative AI tools. Tell beneficiaries when content is made with generative AI, offer a channel that is not automated, and proofread outputs for accuracy. For the public Addressed to developers and users. Follow the Personal Data Protection Law, assess the tool on the four risk levels, label generated content, and verify outputs before relying on them. For Wafi. Rawafid builds and uses a generative AI service, so the public guidelines speak to it directly; it adopts the government ones as its house rule.

slides.title: 131 words that answer nine questions
slides.text: The reference notice, shortened 131 words that answer nine questions "Wafi is Rawafid Schools Group's assistant. It uses generative AI to draft replies to your questions about your child's attendance, lateness and fees. To answer, it reads your child's first name and this term's counts from our records; nothing else is sent. Questions about health, safety, custody, complaints or a disputed fee always go to a member of staff, who replies to you. [...] You may ask a person at any time [...]" The full text adds the basis, the 90-day retention, no sharing outside Rawafid, the rights and the data protection officer's contact.

slides.title: The routing rule needs the words guardians actually write
slides.text: Human review that works in both languages The routing rule needs the words guardians actually write English, Modern Standard Arabic and Gulf Arabic forms for health, harm, disputes, complaints and custody. Leave out words routine questions use: "fee" and "رسوم" would send every balance question to staff. Measure recall per language, and false alarms. Gulf forms that Dana's list missed تعبان · يضايقون · خصمتوا · صك حضانة

slides.title: A review counts only if the reviewer can disagree with the draft
slides.text: Human review A review counts only if the reviewer can disagree with the draft Sees the facts The reviewer reads the guardian's message and the record beside the draft, not the draft alone. Is named Each escalated reply records who approved it. Lab 3.1's accountability check reads that field. Has the time A queue cleared in seconds per reply is approval, not review. That is harm H5. What goes wrong. The draft reads well, so it is approved unread: automation bias, with a person's name on it.

slides.title: The new rule reaches a person for every sensitive enquiry
slides.text: Measured in Lab 3.4 The new rule reaches a person for every sensitive enquiry Rule English recall Arabic recall False alarms Dana's router 8 of 8 2 of 8 0 of 24 The reference rule 8 of 8 8 of 8 0 of 24 Read it carefully. A list that catches all forty has learned these forty. Grow the test set from the messages staff re-route by hand.

slides.title: Which notice meets the guidelines?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which notice meets the guidelines? Layla must choose one line for the foot of every Wafi reply. Which one meets the Generative AI Guidelines' transparency items? "Sent by Wafi, Rawafid's digital service." "This reply may contain errors." "Drafted with AI. Write 'staff' to reach a person." "See our privacy policy for details."

slides.title: The rubric
slides.text: How presentations are scored The rubric Data protection 25% Classification and sharing 20% Risk assessment 20% Ethics tests 20% Disclosure and records 15% Show measured results. A re-identification rate, a fairness gap, a recall per language: a claim without a number is a plan.

slides.title: Ten minutes each: six to present, four for a changed fact
slides.text: Format Ten minutes each: six to present, four for a changed fact 1 · The build Whose data, what it does, where prompts go. One slide or the README. 2 · The pack Walk the repository: registers, code, test report, records, notice. Show the numbers. 3 · The changed fact The assessor changes one fact; you revise the classification and risk entries live. Peer feedback. After each review, everyone writes one strength, one question and one risk they would add.
